extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, associate editors, and editorial board members
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for editors on how to handle situations when peer reviewers give conflicting recommendations for a submitted manuscript (e.g., accept vs. reject), including diagnostic steps and concrete resolution strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the degree and reasons for disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the disagreement is slight (different emphases or approaches) or radical (fundamental differing interpretation), and identify causes such as lack of engagement, misinterpretation, wilful misunderstanding/opposition, or genuinely different careful judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists possible reasons: a referee may not have fully engaged and misinterpreted the content; there may be a wilful misunderstanding because a reviewer opposes the research/methods/viewpoints; or each referee may have independently and carefully come to different conclusions. Use this diagnosis to choose an appropriate resolution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile slight disagreements through clarification or deprioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: If disagreements are slight, reconcile differences by deprioritising one party’s feedback or by following up with the reviewer to confirm engagement and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include treating one reviewer's points as less important relative to others, or undertaking back-and-forth with the reviewer to ensure they have fully engaged with the paper and that you have correctly interpreted their feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise your privilege as editor (make the final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your own assessment, logic, intuition and subject knowledge to make the final decision when reviewers disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor's appointment carries responsibility — you may simply 'make the decision yourself' provided you can back it up with an objective assessment of the paper's merits. Be prepared to justify the decision using your own reading and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get another opinion (appoint a new referee)
rubrics_metrics.description: When conflict is entrenched, appoint an additional referee to break the tie and provide an independent assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose someone you know and trust to provide a robust, impartial and swift review. Keep author timelines in mind — inform the author if they have been waiting a significant time or simply notify them that you need more time to assess the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask a member of the Editorial Board for a tie-breaker review
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask an Editorial Board member to deliver a deciding review when reviewers disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board members typically have a responsibility to assist by providing reviews; they can be a fitting source of an informed, authoritative tie-breaker opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach out to another editor for a second editorial opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult a colleague editor (especially in multi-editor journals) to obtain an additional perspective on the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the consulted editor is not a close subject expert, their objectivity and distance may help resolve the disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask the community for input (use open peer review or discussion forums)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the journal supports open peer review or has a discussion forum in the submission system, solicit wider community input to clarify differences of opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using features such as Editorial Manager’s discussion forum can provide a 'safe' environment for editors and reviewers to discuss the paper and unpick differences. This may be especially useful in journals that operate some form of open peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of author timelines and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: When pursuing additional reviews or discussions to resolve conflicts, consider the author's wait time and whether to inform them of delays or further actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article suggests informing the author if they have already been waiting a significant time, or notifying them that you require more time to assess the manuscript when you appoint extra reviewers or consult others.
